newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK's Allied to create 4,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK's Allied to create 4,000 jobs.

text.p: British drinks group Allied Domecq Plc said on Wednesday that its retailing arm will spend 150 million pounds ($253 million) on a pub development programme that will create up to 4,000 jobs.

Allied Domecq Retailing (ADR), which has over 3,900 managed and leased pubs in Britain, said the programme will involve more than 140 new developments during the next year, including a number of acquisitions.
"The lion's share of the investment will be for the acquisition of new pubs," Martin Grant, managing director of Allied Domecq Leisure, told reporters.
However, these purchases will not produce a significant increase in the number of ADR's pubs given likely sales of existing pubs by the company.
The investment programme will focus on the expansion of the company's three market leading brands - Big Steak Pub with Wacky Warehouse, Firkin and Mr Qs.
ADR plans to expand its family oriented chain of 248 Big Steak Pubs with Wacky Warehouses by 43 in the next year. The pubs offer child minding facilities while harassed parents enjoy a quiet pint.
It aims to convert 24 Allied pubs into Firkin traditional ale pubs to add to its 150-strong Firkin chain and has around 30 acquisitions in the pipeline.
The group will refurbish 40 of its 228-strong Mr Qs chain and spend nine million pounds on converting locals pubs into Mr Qs, aimed at young drinkers.

The majority of the new jobs will be created by the expansion of its Big Steak Pubs and Wacky Warehouse chain, where there are typically around 60 to 70 employees at each outlet. The company said that of the 4,000 new jobs being created over the next 12 months, around 2,200 will be full time with the rest part-time.
Money for the expansion is coming from within the company, with the 150 million pounds roughly in line with the amount spent on development last year.
Allied shares slipped 4.5p to 435p on Wednesday. In a separate statement the company said it would pay its interim dividend as a foreign income dividend (FID).

The company said the move would allow it to claim a refund of 25 million pounds of Advance Corporation Tax paid on the FID. The decision follows changes in the UK Budget last week which abolished the dividend tax credit on ordinary dividends but allowed FIDs to continue until April 1999.
